fire_rating_scale.meaning: minutes the wall keeps the far side from getting too hot

rules.title: Fire zones must not be too big
rules.clause: Chapter II-2, definition of main vertical zones

refs.clause: Directive 2009/45/EC, Annex I, Chapter II-2, Regulation 2 (definitions): main vertical zones

rules.plain_meaning: The ship is cut into sections by fire-resistant walls. On any deck, a section's average length and width should generally not exceed 40 m.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as the first fire walls are placed. Shows each zone's length and width live.
rules.test: For every zone on every deck, measure mean length and mean width.

rules.title: Walls between risky rooms need stronger fire rating
rules.clause: Chapter II-2, tables of fire integrity of divisions (real table depends on room categories and sprinklers)

refs.clause: Directive 2009/45/EC, Annex I, Chapter II-2: tables of fire integrity of bulkheads and decks between adjacent spaces
Directive 2009/45/EC, Annex I, Chapter II-2: main vertical zone boundaries are 'A-60' class divisions

rules.plain_meaning: A wall between two room types must hold back fire for a minimum number of minutes.
rules.early_warning: Runs when a wall is placed between two rooms. Shows the minimum rating needed straight away.
rules.test: For every wall, look up the room pair and compare the wall's minutes with the minimum.
rules.fail_if: wall minutes < minimum for that room pair
rules.assumption_note: Numbers above are placeholders to make the demo work.

rules.title: Two separate ways out

refs.quote: at least two widely separated and ready means of escape shall be provided from all spaces or groups of spaces.
Lifts shall not be considered as forming one of the means of escape
No dead-end corridors having a length of more than 7 m shall be accepted.
Above the bulkhead deck there shall be at least two means of escape from each main vertical zone

refs.clause: Regulation 13, 2.1 ("widely separated"; the 5 m is our working value)
refs.quote: at least two widely separated and ready means of escape

rules.plain_meaning: Every space needs at least two widely separated escape routes. Lifts do not count.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as a room has doors. Shows 'only one way out' right away.
rules.test: From each room, find routes to a stairwell. Count how many are separate (they share no door or corridor piece) and far apart.

values.group_of_spaces_note: Reg 13 2.1 allows 'spaces or groups of spaces'. A cabin with one door onto a corridor is checked as part of that corridor's group.

rules.fail_if: separate routes < 2, or no route reaches an enclosed stairway (unless on the assembly deck), or a dead-end corridor longer than 7 m
rules.assumption_note: The 5 m distance between exits is an assumed placeholder. The document says 'widely separated' with no number. The 7 m dead-end limit is quoted from Reg 13 3.3.4.

rules.title: Escape stairs wide enough
rules.clause: SOLAS II-2/13.3.2.4.5 referring to the FSS Code chapter 13.2.1.1, 13.2.2.2 and 13.2.2.3 (quoted in USCG PRG SOLAS-01); Regulation 13 3.2.1.2 for the 800 mm dispensation case

refs.clause: FSS Code 13.2.1.1, quoted in USCG PRG SOLAS-01
refs.quote: Stairways shall not be less than 900 mm in clear width.
stairways shall not be less than 800 mm in clear width with handrails on both sides.

refs.clause: FSS Code 13.2.2.2, quoted in USCG PRG SOLAS-01
refs.quote: All stairways sized for more than 90 persons shall be aligned fore and aft.
refs.match: fore and aft|fore-aft|athwart|90 persons|across the ship

refs.clause: FSS Code 13.2.2.3, quoted in USCG PRG SOLAS-01
refs.quote: Stairways shall not exceed 3.5 m in vertical rise without the provision of a landing and shall not have an angle of inclination greater than 45.
Corridors and doorways providing access to and from stairways or open decks should be of sufficient width to prevent congestion
The widths, number and continuity of escapes shall be in accordance with the requirements in the Fire Safety Systems Code.
refs.match: no door|top deck|bottom deck|door on|one deck

rules.plain_meaning: Escape stairs must be at least 900 mm wide (FSS Code). Stairs serving more than 90 people must run fore and aft with no curves. A flight may rise at most 3.5 m before a landing, at no more than 45 degrees. 800 mm is only accepted where a single means of escape has been allowed by dispensation (Reg 13 3.2.1.2).
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as a stair is placed. Shows the width against 900 mm and the persons the stair serves.
rules.test: Check width, direction, height of each flight, and handrails on both sides. Also check that the flights fit in the stairwell box (length at the steepest allowed slope, clear width across) and that the stair has a door on its top and bottom deck.

values.fit_note: Model checks, not separate numbers: run needed = rise per flight / tan(max_inclination_deg); with 2 or more flights per deck the flights fold back side by side, so the stairwell must be 2 x clear width across.
values.door_to_stair_clause: Regulation 13 guidance G5.1 (UK MCA copy in docs/): doorways serving stairways should not be less than the width of the stairway

rules.fail_if: width < 900 -> red; more than 90 persons and not aligned fore and aft -> red; rise > 3.5 m -> red; flights do not fit in the stairwell -> red; no door on the top or bottom deck -> amber; emergency door into the stair narrower than the stair -> amber

rules.title: Everyone can get out in time
rules.clause: SOLAS II-2/13.3.2.7; MSC.1/Circ.1533 Annex 1 para 5 (performance standard) and Annex 2 with Appendix 1 (simplified method)

refs.quote: n = 60 if the ship has no more than three main vertical zones and 80, if the ship has more than three main vertical zones.

Congestion points are identified as follows: .1 in those spaces where the initial density is equal, or greater than, 3.5 persons/m2 and .2 in those locations where the difference between inlet and outlet calculated flows (FC ) is in more than 1.5 persons p
GUIDELINES FOR A SIMPLIFIED EVACUATION ANALYSIS FOR NEW AND EXISTING PASSENGER SHIPS
(E+L) should be assumed equal to 30 min.

rules.plain_meaning: Evacuation analysis is mandatory for new passenger ships over 36 passengers with keel laid on or after 1 January 2020. Guidelines say to do it early in design. Total duration 1.25(R+T) + 2/3(E+L) must not exceed n.
rules.early_warning: Grey until rooms, stairs and a muster station exist. Then the simplified Annex 2 calculation runs on every change.
rules.test: Hydraulic model of Annex 2 Appendix 1: corridor density gives initial flow and speed (table 1.1), flows merge at stairs (formula 1.7) and are capped at the maximum specific flow (table 1.2), speeds after transitions from table 1.3. tI = tF + tdeck + tstair + tassembly, T = (gamma + delta) tI.
rules.assumption_note: Values are from the downloaded Circ.1533. Our simplifications: each space follows its shortest route; corridor clear width is taken as the narrowest corridor on the route; stair flights assumed at 45 degrees; E+L defaults to 30 min (Annex 1 5.5).

rules.title: Ship survives flooding

refs.clause: SOLAS II-1 Regulation 6, required subdivision index R (MSC.429(98)/Rev.2 explanatory notes)
refs.quote: REGULATION 6 REQUIRED SUBDIVISION INDEX R

refs.clause: SOLAS II-1 Regulation 7-1, factor p (damage of one or two adjacent zones)
refs.quote: the words "compartment" and "group of compartments" should be understood to mean "zone" and "adjacent
REGULATION 7-3 PERMEABILITY

rules.plain_meaning: The ship's survival score A must be at least the required score R. A adds up, over damage cases, the chance of that damage times the chance of surviving it. R depends on number of people aboard.
rules.early_warning: Runs when two watertight walls exist. Shows compartments and their lengths. Full score appears once the hull and bulkhead deck are set.
rules.test: Flood each single compartment, then each pair of neighbouring compartments. Compute tilt. Mark each case survive or sink. Weight by compartment length. Add up to get A.

required_score_R.N_means: total persons on board, passengers plus crew

values.case_weight: compartment length share of total ship length
values.permeability_note: SOLAS II-1/7-3 table values (the table itself is not in the downloaded MGN 692 annex; confirm).

rules.assumption_note: Heel limit, damage cases, and weights are our simplification. Compartments span the full breadth, so flooding is symmetric. Real calculation uses specialist software. Always label the result 'simplified estimate'.

rules.title: Ship is stable when undamaged
rules.clause: IS Code 2008 Part A, 2.2.1 to 2.2.4 (general criteria)

refs.clause: IS Code 2008 Part A, 2.2.1 to 2.2.4 (general intact stability criteria)

rules.plain_meaning: The righting lever curve (GZ) must give enough area, a large enough maximum at a large enough angle, and a minimum initial GM.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as a hull exists. Every change in rooms or loading moves KG and the GZ curve.
rules.test: Compute GZ by integrating heeled hull sections at constant displacement (fixed trim, hull watertight to the moulded depth) and compare with the criteria.
rules.assumption_note: Criteria values quoted from the IS Code 2008, which is not in docs/. Free-surface correction of slack tanks is included; weather criterion and downflooding angle are not modelled.

rules.title: Enough lifeboats and liferafts
rules.clause: SOLAS III/21.1.1 (passenger ships on international voyages)
rules.plain_meaning: Lifeboats on each side must together carry at least half of everyone on board, and liferafts must carry at least another quarter. They belong on the embarkation deck next to the assembly stations.
rules.early_warning: Grey until the first lifeboat or liferaft is placed. Then capacity per side is compared with the persons on board on every change.
rules.test: Sum lifeboat capacity on each side and liferaft capacity overall; compare with the total persons on board.
rules.fail_if: lifeboat capacity on either side < 50 % of persons, or liferaft capacity < 25 % of persons
rules.assumption_note: Shares quoted from SOLAS III/21.1.1, which is not in docs/. Short international voyage alternatives are not modelled.

rules.title: Ship still floats well if it gets heavier
rules.clause: Section 4.6, Table 8 (design and build margin 160 LT on a 2,350 LT lightship) and section 3.2, Table 1 (service life margin 113 LT on a 2,510 LT lightship), NAVSEA practice

refs.clause: NOAA SWATH report, section 4.6 and Table 8 (design and build margin)
refs.quote: Light ship and deadweight margins conformed with NAVSEA guidelines and criteria.

refs.clause: NOAA SWATH report, section 3.2 and Table 1 (service life margin)
refs.quote: The total deadweight allowance is 980 LT which includes a service life margin of 113 LT.

rules.plain_meaning: Ships get heavier while they are designed, built and used. Designers keep a weight margin: here about 6.8 % of lightship for design and build, plus 4.5 % for growth in service. The ship should still have freeboard and stability with that extra weight.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as the ship floats. Every change in rooms or loading moves the result.
rules.test: Add the margin weight at the lightship centre of gravity, solve the draft again on the hull, and compare the new freeboard and GM with the limits.
rules.fail_if: after the margin weight: deck edge under water or GM below the intact minimum -> red; freeboard below 0.5 m -> amber
rules.assumption_note: Margin shares are from the NOAA report (a 1990 US research ship design following NAVSEA). Meyer Turku may use other margins. The 0.5 m freeboard is the same low-freeboard warning the model check uses. Trim is kept unchanged.

rules.title: Sizes compared with real ships
rules.clause: Smallest values read from three general arrangement drawings in docs/Sources; NOAA report 2.4.2 for rooms used as passageways

refs.clause: General arrangement 23007: 2-person cabins of 15 m2 (7.5 m2 per person)
G.O. Sars general arrangement: decks at 6.30, 9.10, 11.80, 14.30 m (smallest spacing 2.5 m)

refs.quote: Labs should be located so that none serve as general passageways.

rules.plain_meaning: Compares the design with three real research ships: cabins should not be smaller per person than on those ships, decks should not be closer together, and escape routes should not lead through private rooms, work rooms or machinery spaces.
rules.early_warning: Runs on every change. Only gives amber hints; these are good practice, not regulations.
rules.test: Floor area per person of every cabin, height between neighbouring decks, and every escape route checked for rooms it passes through.

values.cabin_area_note: GA 23007: 2-person cabins 15 m2 (7.5 m2 per person), 1-person cabins 12 m2
values.passageway_note: NOAA report 2.4.2: rooms should be located so that none serve as general passageways

rules.fail_if: cabin area per person below 7.5 m2, deck height below 2.5 m, or an escape route passing through a room -> amber
rules.assumption_note: Reference values from research ships, not passenger ship rules. Ferry and cruise cabins can be smaller. Use them as a sanity check only.

rules.title: Fire main reaches every fire zone
rules.clause: SOLAS II-2 Regulation 10, 2.1 fire mains and hydrants

refs.quote: the number and position of hydrants shall be such that the requirements of paragraph 2.1.5.1 may be complied with when all watertight doors and all doors in main vertical zone bulkheads are closed

refs.clause: Regulation 10, 2.1.6.1 (passenger ships of 4,000 gross tonnage and upwards)
refs.quote: 4,000 gross tonnage and upwards 0.40 N/mm
Isolating valves to separate the section of the fire main within the machinery space

rules.plain_meaning: Sea water for fire hoses and sprinklers comes from the fire pumps through the fire main. Every deck with rooms needs the fire main in every fire zone, so hydrants still work when the fire doors between zones are shut, and the pumps must be strong enough to lift the water to the highest hydrant.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as rooms exist. Shows every deck and fire zone without a fire main, fire main pieces not connected to the pumps, and the pump pressure needed for the highest hydrant.
rules.test: For every deck and fire zone with rooms, look for a fire main on that deck inside the zone. Join touching fire main runs; a group is fed when it reaches an engine room (fire pumps). Pump pressure needed = 0.40 N/mm2 + rho g (highest fire main - engine room floor), static head only.
rules.fail_if: a deck and fire zone with rooms has no fire main, or a fire main is not connected to the pumps, or the pressure needed is above the pump pressure -> red; above 90 % of the pump pressure -> amber
rules.assumption_note: The 0.40 N/mm2 hydrant pressure is from Regulation 10 (passenger ships of 4,000 GT and upwards). The 1.2 N/mm2 fire pump delivery pressure is our working value; friction losses in the pipes are not counted.

rules.title: Pipes and cables through watertight bulkheads
rules.clause: SOLAS II-1 Regulation 13.2 (quoted in IACS SDC 8/10/7) and Regulation 12 (collision bulkhead)

refs.clause: SOLAS II-1/12: the collision bulkhead may be pierced below the bulkhead deck by not more than one pipe for the fluid in the forepeak tank, with a screw-down valve operated from above the bulkhead deck

refs.quote: Where pipes, scuppers, electric cables, etc., are carried through watertight bulkheads, arrangements shall be made to ensure the watertight integrity of the bulkheads.
Lead or other heat sensitive materials shall not be used in systems which penetrate watertight bulkheads

rules.plain_meaning: Every pipe or cable through a watertight bulkhead below the bulkhead deck is a possible leak path when the ship is damaged. The collision bulkhead at the bow may only be pierced by one pipe, for the forepeak tank. Hot pipes need heat-proof penetrations.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as pipes or cables cross a watertight bulkhead. Counts the penetrations and flags the collision bulkhead.
rules.test: For every run below the bulkhead deck, find where it crosses a watertight bulkhead. Collision bulkhead = forwardmost watertight bulkhead forward of 70 % of the length.
rules.fail_if: a cable or a pipe other than the forepeak (bilge and ballast) pipe through the collision bulkhead, or more than one pipe -> red; a hot pipe through a watertight bulkhead -> amber
rules.assumption_note: Regulation 12 is not downloaded (summary from Gard); that the forepeak pipe is the bilge and ballast main is our simplification.

rules.title: Fuel oil lines clear of hot surfaces and rooms
rules.clause: IMO MSC/Circ.647 guidelines to minimize leakages from flammable liquid systems (SOLAS II-2/15.2.11, 15.3, 15.4)

refs.quote: There are many potential ignition sources in a machinery space, the most common being hot surfaces, e.g., exhaust pipes and steam pipes.
require oil fuel, lubricating oil and other flammable oil piping to be screened or otherwise suitably protected to avoid as far as practicable oil spray.

rules.plain_meaning: Most engine room fires start when fuel sprays from a leaking joint onto a hot exhaust pipe. Fuel lines should keep well clear of exhaust uptakes, and should not run through cabins, corridors or public rooms where a leak would not be noticed and would endanger people.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as a fuel oil line is drawn. Shows the clear gap to the nearest exhaust and every room the line passes through.
rules.test: Clear gap between the outside of each fuel oil line and each exhaust uptake (3D, centreline distance minus both radii). Rooms of the listed types the fuel line passes through.
rules.fail_if: fuel line touching an exhaust -> red; closer than 1.0 m, or through a listed room -> amber
rules.assumption_note: The circular gives no distance: 1.0 m is our working value for 'clear of hot surfaces'. Keeping fuel lines out of accommodation is good practice we infer from the leak guidance, not a quoted rule.

rules.title: Main cables clear of high fire risk areas
rules.clause: SOLAS II-1 Regulation 45.5.3 (quoted in IACS UI SC11)

refs.clause: SOLAS II-1 Regulation 45.5.3, quoted in IACS UI SC11
refs.quote: Cables and wiring servicing essential or emergency power, lighting, internal communications or signals shall so far as practicable be routed clear of galleys, laundries, machinery spaces of category A and their casings and other high fire risk areas

rules.plain_meaning: Power cables for essential services must not be lost in the fire they are needed for. Main cables should not run through galleys, laundries or other engine rooms, and should keep clear of the exhaust casings that rise from the engine rooms.
rules.early_warning: Runs as soon as a cable is drawn. Lists every galley, laundry or engine room a cable passes through and every exhaust casing it comes close to.
rules.test: Rooms each HV or feeder cable passes through (engine rooms where the cable starts or ends do not count). Clear gap between each cable and each exhaust uptake.
rules.fail_if: a cable through a galley, laundry or another engine room, or closer than 0.5 m to an exhaust casing -> amber ('so far as practicable')
rules.assumption_note: The regulation gives no distance from a casing: 0.5 m is our working value.

questions_for_meyer.Q1: Which fire integrity table do you use for room pairs, and do you want us to follow it exactly? Please share it.
questions_for_meyer.Q2: How far apart must two escape routes be? Is there a number or a design rule you use?
questions_for_meyer.Q3: Stair width: 800 mm (Regulation 13) or 900 mm (FSS Code)? Which do you design to?
questions_for_meyer.Q4: Which evacuation time limit and walking speeds do you use? Can we use a simplified total time for the demo?
questions_for_meyer.Q5: Which flooding survival limits do you want in a simplified check (heel angle, damage cases)? Is it fine to label our result a rough estimate?
questions_for_meyer.Q6: Should the intact stability check follow IS Code 2008 general criteria only, or also the weather criterion and your internal margins?
questions_for_meyer.Q7: Which survival craft arrangement do you design to (SOLAS III/21.1.1 lifeboats 50 % per side plus 25 % liferafts, or a short international voyage / marine evacuation system arrangement)?
questions_for_meyer.Q10: Which weight margins do you use in early design (design and build, service life)? We use 6.8 % and 4.5 % of lightship from the NOAA report.
questions_for_meyer.Q11: What are your smallest cabin areas per person and deck heights for ferries and cruise ships? We compare with three research vessels (7.5 m2 per person, 2.5 m between decks).
questions_for_meyer.Q13: What delivery pressure do your fire pumps have, and do you check the hydrant pressure with friction losses? We use 1.2 N/mm2 at the pump and static head only.
questions_for_meyer.Q14: Which pipes do you route through the collision bulkhead below the bulkhead deck? We allow one forepeak pipe (bilge and ballast main) and nothing else.
questions_for_meyer.Q15: What clear distance do you keep between fuel oil lines and exhaust pipes, and do you allow fuel lines above accommodation? We use 1.0 m and flag fuel lines through rooms.
questions_for_meyer.Q16: Which distance do you keep between main cables and machinery casings, and which spaces do you treat as high fire risk for cable routing? We use 0.5 m and galleys, laundries and engine rooms.
